Method: every Barnes, Ellicott and Pulpit cite (1,563) was fetched from Bible Hub on 2026-10-20 and its verse comment matched by 7-word runs against the archive.org OCR of the named printed volume. 1,536 matched outright. 14 more matched at chapter level. 13 can't be matched because the volumes have no free scan (11 Pulpit Matthew 1 to 11 cites, Pulpit Daniel 7:13). Contributor names were read from title or contents pages, using page images where the OCR lost the gothic type. Keil and Delitzsch and JFB were matched volume by book. Per-cite records are in res\true_authors_percite.json (3,890 rows). res\true_authors_examples.json gives one checkable phrase per writer, with an archive.org search-inside link.

Key results:
1. Barnes (1,046 cites) is four sources. Albert Barnes wrote 684 (NT 443, Job 27, Psalms 79, Isaiah 124, Daniel 11). The rest are other men's:
   - E. B. Pusey, Minor Prophets: 182.
   - J. G. Murphy, Genesis: 31.
   - Speaker's Commentary: 149, split as Rawlinson 30 (1 Kings to Esther), Payne Smith 25 (Jeremiah), Lord Arthur Hervey 22 (Judges, Samuel), Espin 19 (Deuteronomy, Joshua), Currey 16 (Ezekiel), Espin and Thrupp 12 (Numbers), Plumptre 7 (Proverbs), Samuel Clark 6 (Exodus 20 to 40, Leviticus), Bullock 5 (Ecclesiastes), Kingsbury 5 (Song), F. C. Cook 2 (Exodus 1 to 19).
   - Correction to the brief: Exodus is the Speaker's Commentary, not Murphy.
   - Every Bible Hub Barnes page carries the footer "Notes on the Bible by Albert Barnes [1834]. Text Courtesy of Internet Sacred Texts Archive." That footer is the source of the misattribution.
2. Ellicott (264): one named writer per book, from the contributors pages, all 263 matched to the volume. This corrects dates.md: 2 Kings is C. J. Ball (Barry wrote only 1 Kings), and Ezra and Nehemiah are W. B. Pope.
3. Pulpit (253): one expositor per book, read from the title pages (31 rows). This fills dates.md's gaps: Hebrews Barmby, Joel Given, Jonah to Malachi W. J. Deane, Ephesians Blaikie, Colossians Findlay, Philemon Eales, James Gibson, 2 Peter Caffin, Jude Salmond, Ruth Morison. Job's title leaf is missing from the scan and Daniel has no free scan, so those two are unverified. Bible Hub's Pulpit text is BibleSoft's copyrighted digital edition.
4. Keil and Delitzsch (853): Keil 636, Delitzsch 217 (Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, Song, Isaiah), with translators per book (Martin, Bolton, Easton, Harper, Sophia Taylor, Patrick, Kennedy). Bible Hub's Isaiah is the earlier James Martin translation, not the 1890 fourth edition.
5. JFB (855), by the title pages: Jamieson 100 (Genesis to Esther), Fausset 621 (Job to Malachi and 1 Corinthians to Revelation), Brown 134 (Matthew to Romans).
6. Henry: the Revell edition's volume 6 preface lists the continuators. William Tong wrote Revelation (2 cites) and Simon Browne 1 Corinthians (1 cite). The Concise abridger is unnamed, and 26 of its 157 cites abridge the continuators' text, not Henry's.
7. Poole: 26 cites are Poole's own and 57 are by continuators the printed 1685 volume does not name. The 6 Romans cites are Richard Mayo's, per Calamy (1713).
8. Wesley: his own prefaces say the OT notes (197 cites) abridge Matthew Henry and the NT notes (133) translate and abridge Bengel.
9. Church fathers (17): nine writers, two of them anonymous (the Epistle of Barnabas, the Didache).
10. Companion Bible (432): its preface says the edition "is not associated with the name of any man". Which notes were finished after Bullinger's death is not established.

Founder-rule flags, with quotes and sources in authors.md section 5:
- Ecclesiastes: Delitzsch (8 cites), Salmon (Ellicott, 3) and W. J. Deane (Pulpit, 6) each deny that Solomon wrote the book, on the very Bible Hub pages we link.
- F. W. Farrar (13 cites) dated Daniel to 164 BC (Expositor's Bible, 1895).
- O. C. Whitehouse (8 Ellicott Hosea and Amos cites, shared with Reynolds) later taught a Deutero- and Trito-Isaiah.
- A. S. Aglen (12 cites) leaves Jonah open as possible fiction.
- Softer questions: Plumptre (99 cites: Isaiah 36 to 39 given to a disciple, a personated Ecclesiastes), the rest of Delitzsch (Maccabean psalms "possible"), and Ginsburg (Jewish-born Christian, 5 cites).

Cleared with evidence: Pusey, Murphy, Albert Barnes, Bullock, Rawlinson's Pulpit Isaiah (unity), H. Deane's Ellicott Daniel, and W. J. Deane on Zechariah and Jonah.

founderQuestions: Split the 1,046 'Barnes' cites into their true works: Albert Barnes 684, Pusey (Minor Prophets) 182, Murphy (Genesis) 31, and the Speaker's Commentary 149 with a named writer per book? Recommended: yes. The credit names the man who wrote the words and notes that Bible Hub labels the page 'Barnes'.

Ecclesiastes: Delitzsch (8 cites), Salmon (Ellicott, 3) and W. J. Deane (Pulpit, 6) each say on the linked page that Solomon did not write the book. Recommended: remove these 17 cites, or replace them with Bullock or Fausset, who hold that Solomon wrote it, then recount strengths.
F. W. Farrar (Pulpit 1 and 2 Corinthians, Ellicott Judges; 13 cites) dated Daniel to 164 BC in 1895. That is your own example of denying Scripture. Recommended: remove his cites and recount.
O. C. Whitehouse (8 Ellicott Hosea and Amos cites, written jointly with H. R. Reynolds) later taught a Deutero- and Trito-Isaiah. Recommended: remove these joint cites.
A. S. Aglen (Ellicott Psalms 7, Song 4, Jonah 1) leaves Jonah open as possibly fiction. Recommended: remove the Jonah cite, and decide whether his Psalms and Song cites stay.

E. H. Plumptre (99 cites) gives Isaiah 36 to 39 to a disciple and favours a personated Ecclesiastes. Delitzsch's other books (209 cites) allow possible Maccabean psalms. Recommended: keep both, after checking the cites that touch those exact points.
C. D. Ginsburg (Ellicott Leviticus, 5 cites) was a Jewish-born Christian scholar. Recommended: keep him, as with Edersheim.

Wesley's prefaces say his OT notes abridge Matthew Henry and his NT notes translate Bengel. Recommended: credit 'John Wesley, abridging Matthew Henry' (197 OT cites) and 'John Wesley, from Bengel's Gnomon' (133 NT cites).

Henry's Concise (157 cites) has no named abridger, and 26 of its cites abridge Henry's continuators. Recommended: name William Tong and Simon Browne for the 3 full-Henry continuation cites, and replace Concise cites with Henry's full text where he makes the same point.

Poole: 57 cites are by continuators the 1685 volume does not name, and Romans (6) is Richard Mayo's per Calamy. Recommended: credit 'a continuator of Matthew Poole's Annotations (1685), name not printed', and Mayo for Romans.

The Companion Bible (432 cites) was printed with no author's name. Recommended: credit 'The Companion Bible (1909 to 1922), notes generally attributed to E. W. Bullinger' until the parts finished after his death are identified.
Bible Hub's Pulpit text is BibleSoft's copyrighted digital edition. Recommended: quote Pulpit words from the archive.org scans named in authors.md.

design.creditExample: James G. Murphy (Presbyterian minister and Professor of Hebrew, Belfast), Commentary on Genesis, Andover edition of 1866, on Genesis 2:7. Read on Bible Hub, which labels it “Barnes’ Notes”; retrieved 20 October 2026. Read it there ›  ("Read it there" opens https://biblehub.com/commentaries/barnes/genesis/2.htm, the page the mend record for genesis-2-7 note 1 fetched on 2026-10-20. The year shows 1866, the earliest dated printing read, criticalexeg00murp. It becomes 1863 only once the Edinburgh first edition is read. The "about" phrase is checked against that printing's title page and its preface to the American edition.)
founderQuestions: When a writer's introduction to a book denies Scripture, is he dropped the way Aglen was? Aglen's words ('if it is the creation of fiction') are in his introduction on Bible Hub's Ellicott Jonah 1 page. The app cites his comments on Jonah 4:6 (1), the Psalms (7) and the Song of Solomon (4), and decision 20 drops all 12. Delitzsch, George Salmon and W. J. Deane each say in their own introduction to Ecclesiastes that Solomon did not write it. The app cites their comments on Ecclesiastes 3 to 7 (17 cites) and on their other books (Delitzsch 209 more, Deane 44 more). Recommended: keep Aglen dropped as ruled. For these three, judge each cited comment on its own words and leave out any Ecclesiastes comment that itself treats the Teacher as someone other than Solomon. This follows decision 2 (Luther is kept while his denying prefaces are left out) and decision 20 ('leave out only passages that deny it'). The earlier shortlist answer that kept Keil and Delitzsch and the Pulpit Commentary off Ecclesiastes stays a rule only for the Christian writers at Deep, where whole notes, introductions included, are shown word for word.

When strengths are counted, should a writer who abridges another count as that writer? Wesley's own 1765 preface says his Old Testament notes abridge Matthew Henry, and his 1755 preface says his New Testament notes translate and abridge Bengel. The Concise Commentary abridges Henry. Recommended: yes, count each abridgment as the writer it abridges. On the notes as they stand, this lowers 5 notes from 'widely agreed' to 'commonly held' (Genesis 17:15, 29:25, 32:30 and 35:7, and 2 Kings 2:23, each note 1) unless a third writer is found. It also changes the wording of the CLAUDE.md strength rule from 'a distinct cited work' to 'a person who wrote the cited words'.
